author: Christer Lundin
releaseNotes:
v1.5.0: Move an area from a dashboard button. Each area device now has a button (Momentary and PushableButton): pushing it moves that area to your phone's last reported position. Off unless you turn on 'Allow this hub to move areas' in the app AND your API key was created with 'Allow this key to move areas you created' at dev.positionguardai.com (existing keys can't gain it — create a new one). Only areas you created can be moved; every area device shows the button, and on an area you didn't create PositionGuard's refusal is shown. The hub never sends or receives coordinates — the request has no body and the answer is a distance — but the area's new centre is visible to your group, as any area's is. Two new attributes on area devices: lastMoveResult (a readable sentence — the outcome, or PositionGuard's refusal word for word) and lastMoveAt (when the area last actually moved). A refused move never affects polling or presence devices.

v1.4.1: positionFresh now tells the truth when PositionGuard holds a member at a saved place. When a phone goes quiet inside one of the member's places, PositionGuard keeps safetyStatus at 'at_area' instead of flapping to 'unknown'; positionFresh now reads 'false' during that hold (it read 'true' before), and the event log says '<name> was last confirmed at a saved place <age> ago', with the age in minutes under 90 min ('45 min ago') and in hours after, to one decimal when not whole ('10 h ago', '2.5 h ago'). Rules that must know someone is there right now should also require positionFresh 'true'. No new attributes; presence and currentArea are unchanged.

v1.4.0: Per-area member counts — each area in a group now gets a device reporting how many members are currently inside it, plus a count of members whose position is stale. Coordinate-free: the device reports how many, never where. Useful for occupancy rules — a count of 0 is a reliable 'everyone's out' trigger.

Behavior change: safetyStatus now reports 'unknown' when a member's position has gone stale, instead of 'stale'. A phone that hasn't reported recently is genuinely unknown, and treating it as a location was producing rules that fired on someone who hadn't moved. If you have a rule comparing safetyStatus directly to 'out_of_zone', it will no longer match during stale periods — outsideUsualArea is unaffected and remains strictly true/false.

Two new attributes: positionAgeSeconds and positionFresh, so rules can gate on data freshness directly. Existing devices may need opening the device page once for the new attributes to appear.

Fixed: an out_of_zone transition logged its message twice per poll.
